v.rationale:
All three pass their own suites (impl-1 10 tests, impl-2 20, impl-3 16). I got the MySQL DDL from `pretend()` because no MySQL server was reachable, then ran probes on SQLite: an empty `?status=`, rollback followed by re-migrate, sparse ids with mixed-case and padded emails, and ordering when created_at ties. The probes were deleted afterwards. All three backfills are the same basically sound set-based UPDATE over id ranges with whereNull and EXISTS. None of them changes updated_at, and none touches unmatched orders.

impl-1 had no bugs in the probes. It handles the large-table part best: explicit INSTANT/INPLACE LOCK=NONE DDL, indexes built before the FK, a correct down(), and both query shapes indexed. It loses idiom points for raw driver-branched DDL that the test suite never runs, for making customer_id fillable, and for thinner tests.

impl-2 has the best Eloquent idioms and tests, but its down() leaves the composite indexes behind. Rollback fails on SQLite, and on MySQL it leaves shrunken indexes whose names block re-migration. It also builds a throwaway implicit FK index over 20M rows.

impl-3 has the neatest backfill code, but its FormRequest rejects `?status=` with a 422. That changes behaviour on the hot production endpoint in exactly the call shape the task names. It also uses after(), which can force a table rebuild before MySQL 8.0.29, has a single index that doesn't suit the unfiltered query, and has no tie-breaker.

Weighting real bugs heavily: impl-3's user-facing regression ranks below impl-2's rollback-only bug, and impl-1, the only one without a found bug, ranks first.
